BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every core protection. Taken together, the changes would cut our recovery to a fraction of what the playbook requires. The package also leaves three Completion-critical items unresolved: Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms each of those gaps. I recommend we reject the package framing and return a full mark-up on our starting positions.

---

## 1. Threshold issue: the "[STANDARD] / FINAL" framing

The cover document says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are marked FINAL, and that clauses tagged [STANDARD] "need no further scrutiny."

**I have not accepted that framing, and I recommend we don't either.**

- It is the Seller's own characterisation in an untrusted draft. We have no record of any agreement.
- Several "[STANDARD]" positions are exactly the fallbacks our playbook reserves for Amelia Frost's prior written authority, such as the 20% cap and 18 months. **No such authority has been given.** If these had been agreed at principal level, a written approval from Amelia identifying this draft would exist.
- The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not a term. Market norms do not override our mandate.
- Tagging the most buyer-adverse clauses as "no scrutiny needed" is a reason to review them more closely, not less.

**Action:** Ask Amelia to confirm that she has not agreed any of these positions. Reply to Seller counsel that nothing in the draft is agreed until it appears in an executed SPA.

---

## 2. Liability regime

| Item | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap / push-back |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** | 20% is our conditional fallback and needs Amelia's written authority, which we don't have. Table 25%. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | **AUD 5,000** | 5x our position. Individually modest claims would fall away. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | **AUD 50,000, first dollar** | Double hit: the threshold is 5x higher, and the "excess only" structure turns it into a permanent AUD 250k deductible. Insist on a tipping basket. |
| General claims period | 18 months | **24 months** | 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's approval (none). 24 months gives two audit cycles. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" (cl 12.3/13) | Seller proposes | Categories kept separate; no hidden override | **High priority.** This default sweeps fundamental, tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity claims into the general regime unless each carve-out is perfectly drafted. Reverse it: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated. |

### Fundamental / Title warranties
The Seller wants capacity and title on the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." **Reject.** Title is the asset we are paying AUD 24m for. Playbook position:
- 100% of price
- At least six years
- Outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar

### Fraud, and the "all Claims of any nature" limitations (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
Applying the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses to "all Claims of any nature" would, on its face, extend them to fraud and wilful concealment. **This is non-negotiable for us.** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
- caps
- baskets
- time limits
- exclusive remedy
- non-reliance

No one on our side has authority to waive this. Any non-reliance clause also needs a fraud carve-out, so that it does not undercut misrepresentation claims grounded in fraud.

### Tax and IP
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime above." **They are not settled.** Our playbook treats Tax and IP as OPEN, separate categories. We should not let them fold into the general cap or period by assertion. We also should not imply we are seeking unlimited liability. Respond that the terms remain open for negotiation as separate regimes.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

These two clauses combine to hollow out the warranties and even the specific indemnities.

### General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. **Reject.** We require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail for us to assess nature and scope.
- Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to the specific items in paragraphs 2–10, and only to the extent each is fairly disclosed.
- The data room is fixed "as at 22 September 2026." It is now November. Confirm whether anything has been added or changed since, and ensure no rolling or deemed update operates.
- **Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission)** is acceptable as a concept. It must not be used to argue that a specifically disclosed problem (for example, the unrepaid Riverlark facility) relieves the Seller of obligations to fix it.

### Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)
The Seller's clause excludes claims for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **or that was discoverable** from the data room or public records. This is the broadest possible form. **Delete it.**

Critically, the Disclosure Letter itself tells us about the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus and DD-006 issues. Under cl 8.3 as drafted, our knowledge of those issues could defeat claims on exactly the matters we are negotiating specific protection for.

If any qualifier survives, it must:
- use **named Seller knowledge persons** and **reasonable enquiry**, and
- **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 4. Completion-critical items

### Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): high priority
- Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. That makes it the single largest commercial risk to value.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. Under our playbook that is insufficient on both counts.
- Disclosure paragraph 2 confirms that no final consent has been given and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. So the "[STANDARD] … addressed" label is inaccurate on the Seller's own disclosure.
- **Push for** a condition precedent requiring an *effective* consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, all before Completion. The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer.

### Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): high priority
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with a change-control provision at cl 8.1. Disclosure paragraph 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in hand.
- A release "to be provided following Completion" means we would complete into a company with a live change-of-control trigger and security over its assets.
- **Push for:**
  - a current payout letter
  - repayment directly from Completion funds as a funds-flow line (consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing)
  - executed, effective security releases (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion
- A post-Completion release is acceptable **only** with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia's approval. Neither exists.

### Employee bonuses (funds flow): high priority
- DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. The Seller states they are "a matter for the Seller" but deliberately leaves them out of the funds flow. That is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits.
- If the Company is the payer, the cost lands on us after Completion. That is value leakage on a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- Disclosure paragraph 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Push for** a specific funds-flow line item (or treatment as Debt), or express Seller funding, covering the AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs**. We should not put a number on the on-costs until they are confirmed. Also confirm who bears the bonuses if the continued-employment conditions are not met.

---

## 5. Specific risk items

### Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- The current indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Disclosure paragraph 4 confirms there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open. That figure is **not independently verified in either direction**, so we should not treat it as the confirmed exposure or as confirmed nil.
- **Push to broaden** the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own or validly use the Ironquay/SOW3 materials, and any Ironquay claim relating to them.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Ideally make these Completion deliverables.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

### DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- We should not accept the Seller's view that this is "not expected to be material."
- Equally, we should not characterise it as a confirmed breach. On the disclosed material there is no confirmed access, harm, notification obligation or loss amount. The record is a download link sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records, with the investigation still preliminary.
- **Push for** covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and its expiry or revocation
  - give the Buyer regular updates and the right to review findings before Completion
  - make no regulator or individual notifications without consulting the Buyer, subject to legal obligations
- Consider specific protection if the investigation reveals exposure. Make no numeric demand at this stage.

### Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)
- The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs." We should neither accept that nor reclassify them as Debt or a price deduction automatically.
- Disclosure paragraph 8 says the three AUD 110,000 renewals should be "read together" and are silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. That warrants diligence.
- **Ask:**
  - Why were three related renewals of equal size entered into?
  - What are the timing and term of each?
  - Can they be terminated, and on what terms?
  - Are any amounts prepaid or accrued at Completion?
  - Were they approved in the ordinary course?
- Decide the treatment once we have the answers.

### Title (DD-012)
- The share register is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof. Disclosure paragraph 10 concedes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Require independent evidence**, which could include:
  - a current ASIC company extract reconciled to the register
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption and transfer restrictions)
  - share certificates or confirmation of no certificates
  - PPSR and other encumbrance searches over the shares
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights to issue shares
- Back all of this with the fundamental-warranty regime in section 2.

### Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller characterises these as notification-only, with no consent needed for a share sale. That may be right, but it is the Seller's reading. **We should check the underlying DD-007 and DD-009 provisions ourselves**, including any change-of-control definitions. Make any required notifications a Completion deliverable.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

**Process**
1. Reject the "[STANDARD] / FINAL / no further scrutiny" framing and the market-context preamble. Confirm with Amelia Frost that nothing has been agreed and that no fallback authority has been given.

**Liability package: revert to playbook starting positions**

2. Cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m (not 20%).
3. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery (not AUD 25k/250k, excess only).
4. General claims period: 24 months (not 18).
5. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims, as expressly stated.
6. Fundamental/Title: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
7. Carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision. This is non-negotiable.
8. Tax and IP: OPEN, as separate regimes, not folded into the general regime.

**Disclosure and knowledge**

9. Delete general data-room and public-record disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2). Require specific, fair disclosure only.
10. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3). Any qualifier must use named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or the specific indemnities.

**Completion mechanics**

11. Bluefen: CP for effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are not enough.
12. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
13. Bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded. No silent exclusion.

**Specific risks**

14. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure (cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment), and treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified.
15. DD-006: covenants for log preservation, investigation and updates. No breach characterisation and no numeric demand.
16. Sandbar: diligence questions first. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
17. Title: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.
18. Lease and Mossvale: verify the underlying clauses independently and make notifications Completion deliverables.

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
- (1) fraud carve-out and the "all Claims" override
- (2) Bluefen, Riverlark and bonuses
- (3) fundamental/title regime
- (4) disclosure and buyer knowledge
- (5) cap, thresholds and period
- (6) the specific risk items

I can prepare the mark-up of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5 and a response note to Seller counsel on that basis, if helpful.

- Disclosure paragraph 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Push for** a specific funds-flow line item (or treatment as Debt), or express Seller funding, covering the AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs**. We should not put a number on the on-costs until they are confirmed. Also confirm who bears the bonuses if the continued-employment conditions are not met.

## 5. Specific risk items

### Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- The current indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Disclosure paragraph 4 confirms there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open. That figure is **not independently verified in either direction**, so we should not treat it as the confirmed exposure or as confirmed nil.
- **Push to broaden** the indemnity to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own or validly use the Ironquay/SOW3 materials, and any Ironquay claim relating to them.
- **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Ideally make these Completion deliverables.
- Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

### DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- We should not accept the Seller's view that this is "not expected to be material."
- Equally, we should not characterise it as a confirmed breach. On the disclosed material there is no confirmed access, harm, notification obligation or loss amount. The record is a download link sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records, with the investigation still preliminary.
- **Push for** covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence
  - complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and its expiry or revocation
  - give the Buyer regular updates and the right to review findings before Completion
  - make no regulator or individual notifications without consulting the Buyer, subject to legal obligations
- Consider specific protection if the investigation reveals exposure. Make no numeric demand at this stage.

### Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)
- The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs." We should neither accept that nor reclassify them as Debt or a price deduction automatically.
- Disclosure paragraph 8 says the three AUD 110,000 renewals should be "read together" and are silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. That warrants diligence.
- **Ask:**
  - Why were three related renewals of equal size entered into?
  - What are the timing and term of each?
  - Can they be terminated, and on what terms?
  - Are any amounts prepaid or accrued at Completion?
  - Were they approved in the ordinary course?
- Decide the treatment once we have the answers.

### Title (DD-012)
- The share register is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof. Disclosure paragraph 10 concedes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Require independent evidence**, which could include:
  - a current ASIC company extract reconciled to the register
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption and transfer restrictions)
  - share certificates or confirmation of no certificates
  - PPSR and other encumbrance searches over the shares
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights to issue shares
- Back all of this with the fundamental-warranty regime in section 2.

### Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller characterises these as notification-only, with no consent needed for a share sale. That may be right, but it is the Seller's reading. **We should check the underlying DD-007 and DD-009 provisions ourselves**, including any change-of-control definitions. Make any required notifications a Completion deliverable.
